candidates.title: Don't append weak-retriever API docs to a model not trained for retrieval
candidates.rule: If a model was fine-tuned (or prompted) without retrieval for API selection, do not append top-1 BM25 or embedding-retrieved API documentation at inference; keep it zero-shot unless the retriever is near-oracle.
candidates.passage: The result illustrates that adding a non-optimal retriever at test time will sometime misguide the model and result in more errors.
candidates.finding: Gorilla fine-tuned without a retriever scored 59.13 (TorchHub), 71.68 (HuggingFace), 83.79 (TensorHub) zero-shot, but dropped to 37.63/11.28/34.30 with BM25 and 60.21/28.10/52.40 with GPT-Index; hallucination also rose with BM25 on HuggingFace (10.95 to 46.46).
workloads: APIBench: TorchHub, HuggingFace, TensorFlow Hub API-call selection, AST sub-tree matching
candidates.conditions: Top-1 retrieved document only, concatenated with the fixed prefix 'Use this API documentation for reference:'; single-line API call generation; no further prompt tuning.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, 2023 model checkpoints, ML model-hub APIs only; top-1 retrieval is a weak setup and multi-document retrieval was not tested; for GPT-3.5/GPT-4 the GPT-Index retriever actually improved accuracy, so the effect is model-dependent.
candidates.validation_test: On your own API catalogue, evaluate the same model zero-shot vs. with top-1 retrieved docs, scoring correct API selection and hallucination rate; also test top-k retrieval before concluding retrieval hurts.

candidates.title: Verify tool calls by AST sub-tree matching against an API registry
candidates.rule: To score and gate generated API calls, parse the output into an AST and check that the call node plus a declared set of required arguments form a sub-tree of a registry entry; treat non-matching calls as hallucinated tools rather than relying on execution tests.
candidates.passage: We define a hallucination as an API call that is not a sub-tree of any API in the database – invoking an entirely imagined tool.
candidates.finding: The authors used this metric to measure all reported accuracies and hallucination rates, arguing unit tests cannot verify semantically equivalent API choices. Using it as a runtime guard before dispatch is our extrapolation; the paper evaluates but does not deploy it as a filter.
workloads: APIBench evaluation of single-line Python API calls
candidates.conditions: Single API call per response; optional arguments (e.g. pretrained=True) excluded from matching; required arguments specified per API (e.g. repo_or_dir, model for torch.hub.load).
candidates.limitations: Only validated on single-call, single-line Python outputs over three ML model hubs; it checks identity against a registry, not functional or runtime correctness; the HuggingFace registry is non-exhaustive, so non-Gorilla models were scored only on domain, weakening cross-model comparability.
candidates.validation_test: Implement the AST sub-tree check over your tool registry, run it on logged agent calls, and compare its hallucination labels against manual review plus actual execution failures.

reason: The paper reports matched comparisons of fine-tuning with/without retrieval and of appending retrieved API docs at test time across four retriever settings, yielding two scoped, actionable rules. A third rule about retriever-match between training and inference is inferred from the same tables.
